answer: Rotating Ridge Committees. Each epoch, a verifiable random function seeded by a public beacon assigns identities to small review committees; assignment is unpredictable until the seed is published, so attackers cannot pre-position sybils on favorable panels. To steer outcomes, an attacker must control many identities across many unpredictable committees, so each additional identity raises expected infiltration cost. A nebula of decoy panels absorbs cheap probes, and a jade audit layer recomputes assignments to catch manipulation.
